Expo/React Native iOS + Android client. Pure OAuth API consumer of the web contract.

rulings.text: Three answers: (1) Currency: UK gets GBP, France and other European countries get EUR. (2) Trial cap behavior: hard stop on AI/LLM features once the $10/month cap is hit — no more AI features until next billing month or the tenant upgrades. (3) Design: loop design in now, from the start, not after web starts building — note Stripe is typically integrated as an iframe within existing UI (not a full redirect).

Cancellation timing: run-to-end-of-current-billing-period (web's recommendation) — access stays at the paid tier until the period the tenant already paid for ends, then reverts to the trial's $10/month cap. No proration refunds. Design builds the cancel-confirmation UI reflecting this wording next, web implements once design delivers.

DECIDE 1: A — honour last-known entitlement offline, unbounded, re-read on every successful reconnect (web+mobile's joint recommendation, adopted as-is). DECIDE 2: B — every tenant gets a fresh 90-day trial from the enforcement-launch date, as the standing rule; this applies to the dogfood households too, not a permanent grandfather. Additional requirement: JF wants the dogfood households to go through the REAL trial-to-paid Stripe flow end to end, not skip it — but at a steep discount via a Stripe discount/coupon code: $1/month or $10/year instead of the real $20/mo or $180/yr. JF's words: 'I guess there will be some charges with Stripe, but I believe it worths the test.' He accepts the small real charges as the cost of testing the actual payment path. Build the checkout to accept/apply a discount code; the Stripe-side coupon creation itself is a JF/ops action in the Stripe dashboard, not a web build task.

DECIDE 3: B, unified across trial-expired and cancelled-lapsed (this SUPERSEDES the earlier cancel-ruling's '/month trial cap' wording, which was ambiguous — B is the actual behavior). JF's words: 'the application continues to function except for all the AI functions from prediction, to ingestion, to interpretation, to chat. On the chat, stating the trial is expired, or you have canceled the subscription, and stating you can subscribe to reactivate your subscription and providing a link to the setting billing page where the use can activate or re-activate their subscription.' So: non-AI app functionality (tasks, ledger, views, everything not AI-driven) keeps working normally for a non-paying tenant, whether trial-expired or cancelled-and-lapsed. All AI-surfaced functions go off: prediction, ingestion, interpretation, chat. The chat surface specifically stays reachable but shows an explanatory state (trial expired / subscription cancelled) plus a link to settings/billing where the tenant can (re)activate.

Explicit ruling: no credit card is required to start the 90-day trial — an account/tenant is created and the trial begins with no Stripe interaction at all. A credit card / Stripe checkout is only requested when the tenant chooses to subscribe: at day 90 to continue past the trial, or on an earlier voluntary upgrade. Abuse-control against this stays whatever the existing account-creation gates already provide (invitation code, demo-passcode restrictions, rate limits) — no card-based friction is added.

PRICING AND CURRENCY. This SUPERSEDES the currency part of the 2026-09-11 ruling on q-20260911-004 (UK GBP / Europe EUR / USA USD / Canada CAD), and the "same numeral in every currency" line in the #2018 setup checklist.

JF's words, verbatim, 2026-09-25:
1. What he set up in Stripe (test mode): "I created only one currency in CAD domi standard it's 30 monthly, and 250 yearly, and domi plus 50 monthly, and 500 yearly"
2. What he asked for: "can we have one pricing in CAD, and depending the country you are, you pay with the convertion at that time, so if you are coming from US, you are presented with 21.21 USD for the domi standard monthly"
3. His ruling, choosing option A (one CAD price list, converted by Stripe Adaptive Pricing): "Let's go with A, and the adaptive pricing for now. We'll upgrade if the product is successful to their own currency"

What this means for the build. Chief's reading; verify against Stripe's docs (docs.stripe.com/payments/currencies/localize-prices/adaptive-pricing):
- Prices exist in CAD only: Standard C$30/mo and C$250/yr, Plus C$50/mo and C$500/yr. They must NOT carry currency_options. A local-currency option on a price stops Adaptive Pricing converting to that currency.
- Adaptive Pricing works only with Stripe Checkout Sessions (hosted, embedded page or embedded form). Stripe: "Adaptive Pricing isn't available for businesses using Elements with the Payment Intents API." The #2019 checkout must use Checkout Sessions.
- The currency-by-region logic in #2019 is no longer needed. Stripe picks the presentment currency.
- The customer pays Stripe's 2-4% conversion fee. Local amounts are non-round and follow the exchange rate. For customers outside Canada, subscriptions accept only cards, Link, Apple Pay and Google Pay.
- JF enables Adaptive Pricing himself in the Stripe Dashboard (Settings > Payments > Adaptive Pricing), in test mode first.
- The dogfood coupons are now fixed amounts off in CAD, restricted to Domi Standard, duration Forever: C$29 off monthly (C$30 becomes C$1) and C$240 off yearly (C$250 becomes C$10). This replaces the 95%-off coupon in the checklist. Chief proposed these amounts to JF; JF has not stated them himself.
- Local-currency prices ("their own currency") are deferred, not cancelled: "We'll upgrade if the product is successful".
- Price IDs, product IDs and the publishable key follow when JF pastes them.

COUPON, correcting chief's proposal in the previous ruling. JF's words, verbatim, 2026-09-25: "the coupon 95% and the promotion code are created." So the dogfood coupon in Stripe test mode is a 95%-off coupon with a promotion code, NOT the C$29 / C$240 fixed amounts chief proposed. Chief's arithmetic, not JF's words: on the CAD prices, 95% off gives C$1.50/mo on Standard monthly and C$12.50/yr on Standard yearly. The promotion-code text follows when JF pastes it.

JF's words, verbatim, 2026-09-25: "keep the current pricing, the webhook have been setup for staging webhook." (1) WEBHOOK: JF has set up the Stripe test-mode webhook for staging. Per the checklist it points at https://staging.domiapp.ai/api/stripe/webhook with the five events (customer.subscription.created/updated/deleted, invoice.paid, invoice.payment_failed); chief has not seen the dashboard, so confirm the URL and events against what #2020 serves. The signing secret goes into Vercel staging by JF, never through an agent. (2) PRICING: chief's reading, not JF's words. 'Current pricing' = what is already set up and specced in #2108 (CAD C$30/C$250 and C$50/C$500, Adaptive Pricing, the 95%-off coupon), which JF is confirming unchanged. It does NOT answer the four open DECIDEs (design copy task, upgrade proration, sales tax, past_due); those are still with JF.

UPGRADE Standard -> Plus (answers open DECIDE 'upgrade proration'). JF's words, verbatim, 2026-09-25: "for upgrsding from standr to plus, you charge the difference when that is happening, and it's the new renewal subscripption date". So: charge at the moment of upgrade, and the upgrade date becomes the new renewal date (the billing cycle restarts). CHIEF'S READING in Stripe terms, to verify, not JF's words: subscription update with billing_cycle_anchor=now plus immediate proration invoicing. The customer pays the full Plus period minus a credit for the unused part of Standard. Example: halfway through a C$30 Standard month, the upgrade costs C$50 - C$15 = C$35, and the next renewal is one month after the upgrade day. As far as chief knows, the Stripe customer portal cannot reset the cycle anchor on a same-interval switch, so #2021 may need its own upgrade call rather than portal plan switching. Verify against Stripe's docs. Not covered by this ruling: monthly <-> yearly switches and Plus -> Standard downgrades.

SALES TAX (answers spec §9.2). JF's words, verbatim, 2026-09-25: "sales tax, for now no tax if possible". So: build with NO tax. No Stripe Tax, and no tax lines at checkout. CHIEF'S NOTES, not JF's words: (a) 'for now': keep tax switch-on-able later without re-creating prices, and do not bake a tax assumption into the prices or the UI copy. (b) 'if possible' is a legal condition chief cannot verify. Canadian GST/HST registration is generally required only above the C$30k/yr small-supplier threshold, but with Adaptive Pricing selling abroad, the EU and UK may expect VAT from a foreign seller's first consumer sale. JF will confirm with his accountant before live mode. This does not block the test-mode build.

JF's words, verbatim, 2026-09-25: "A, A, A". Answering the three DECIDEs as chief put them to him:

1. FAILED RENEWAL / past_due (spec §9.1). Chose A: "keep AI on while Stripe retries the card, and cut it off when Stripe gives up". That is web's recommendation: treat past_due as active while Stripe's automatic retries run, and let customer.subscription.deleted make the tenant canceled. Chief told JF to set, in the Stripe Dashboard, Settings > Billing > Revenue recovery > Retries > "if all retries fail: cancel the subscription". That is what makes Stripe giving up end the subscription. Chief has not seen whether JF set it; verify it in test mode.

2. MONTHLY <-> YEARLY SWITCH. Chose A: handled like an upgrade. Charge now, minus a credit for the unused time, and the switch date becomes the new renewal date.

3. PLUS -> STANDARD DOWNGRADE. Chose A: takes effect at the next renewal, with no refund. Plus stays until the end of the paid period, consistent with the no-proration-refund cancellation ruling of 2026-09-12.

The fourth "A" in chief's list (file design's expired/capped/cancelled copy task) is being filed by chief as a separate queue task for design.

rulings.text: Cancellation timing: run-to-end-of-current-billing-period (web's recommendation) — access stays at the paid tier until the period the tenant already paid for ends, then reverts to the trial's $10/month cap. No proration refunds. Design builds the cancel-confirmation UI reflecting this wording next, web implements once design delivers.

DECIDE 1: A — honour last-known entitlement offline, unbounded, re-read on every successful reconnect (web+mobile's joint recommendation, adopted as-is). DECIDE 2: B — every tenant gets a fresh 90-day trial from the enforcement-launch date, as the standing rule; this applies to the dogfood households too, not a permanent grandfather. Additional requirement: JF wants the dogfood households to go through the REAL trial-to-paid Stripe flow end to end, not skip it — but at a steep discount via a Stripe discount/coupon code: $1/month or $10/year instead of the real $20/mo or $180/yr. JF's words: 'I guess there will be some charges with Stripe, but I believe it worths the test.' He accepts the small real charges as the cost of testing the actual payment path. Build the checkout to accept/apply a discount code; the Stripe-side coupon creation itself is a JF/ops action in the Stripe dashboard, not a web build task.

DECIDE 3: B, unified across trial-expired and cancelled-lapsed (this SUPERSEDES the earlier cancel-ruling's '/month trial cap' wording, which was ambiguous — B is the actual behavior). JF's words: 'the application continues to function except for all the AI functions from prediction, to ingestion, to interpretation, to chat. On the chat, stating the trial is expired, or you have canceled the subscription, and stating you can subscribe to reactivate your subscription and providing a link to the setting billing page where the use can activate or re-activate their subscription.' So: non-AI app functionality (tasks, ledger, views, everything not AI-driven) keeps working normally for a non-paying tenant, whether trial-expired or cancelled-and-lapsed. All AI-surfaced functions go off: prediction, ingestion, interpretation, chat. The chat surface specifically stays reachable but shows an explanatory state (trial expired / subscription cancelled) plus a link to settings/billing where the tenant can (re)activate.

Explicit ruling: no credit card is required to start the 90-day trial — an account/tenant is created and the trial begins with no Stripe interaction at all. A credit card / Stripe checkout is only requested when the tenant chooses to subscribe: at day 90 to continue past the trial, or on an earlier voluntary upgrade. Abuse-control against this stays whatever the existing account-creation gates already provide (invitation code, demo-passcode restrictions, rate limits) — no card-based friction is added.

PRICING AND CURRENCY. This SUPERSEDES the currency part of the 2026-09-11 ruling on q-20260911-004 (UK GBP / Europe EUR / USA USD / Canada CAD), and the "same numeral in every currency" line in the #2018 setup checklist.

JF's words, verbatim, 2026-09-25:
1. What he set up in Stripe (test mode): "I created only one currency in CAD domi standard it's 30 monthly, and 250 yearly, and domi plus 50 monthly, and 500 yearly"
2. What he asked for: "can we have one pricing in CAD, and depending the country you are, you pay with the convertion at that time, so if you are coming from US, you are presented with 21.21 USD for the domi standard monthly"
3. His ruling, choosing option A (one CAD price list, converted by Stripe Adaptive Pricing): "Let's go with A, and the adaptive pricing for now. We'll upgrade if the product is successful to their own currency"

What this means for the build. Chief's reading; verify against Stripe's docs (docs.stripe.com/payments/currencies/localize-prices/adaptive-pricing):
- Prices exist in CAD only: Standard C$30/mo and C$250/yr, Plus C$50/mo and C$500/yr. They must NOT carry currency_options. A local-currency option on a price stops Adaptive Pricing converting to that currency.
- Adaptive Pricing works only with Stripe Checkout Sessions (hosted, embedded page or embedded form). Stripe: "Adaptive Pricing isn't available for businesses using Elements with the Payment Intents API." The #2019 checkout must use Checkout Sessions.
- The currency-by-region logic in #2019 is no longer needed. Stripe picks the presentment currency.
- The customer pays Stripe's 2-4% conversion fee. Local amounts are non-round and follow the exchange rate. For customers outside Canada, subscriptions accept only cards, Link, Apple Pay and Google Pay.
- JF enables Adaptive Pricing himself in the Stripe Dashboard (Settings > Payments > Adaptive Pricing), in test mode first.
- The dogfood coupons are now fixed amounts off in CAD, restricted to Domi Standard, duration Forever: C$29 off monthly (C$30 becomes C$1) and C$240 off yearly (C$250 becomes C$10). This replaces the 95%-off coupon in the checklist. Chief proposed these amounts to JF; JF has not stated them himself.
- Local-currency prices ("their own currency") are deferred, not cancelled: "We'll upgrade if the product is successful".
- Price IDs, product IDs and the publishable key follow when JF pastes them.

COUPON, correcting chief's proposal in the previous ruling. JF's words, verbatim, 2026-09-25: "the coupon 95% and the promotion code are created." So the dogfood coupon in Stripe test mode is a 95%-off coupon with a promotion code, NOT the C$29 / C$240 fixed amounts chief proposed. Chief's arithmetic, not JF's words: on the CAD prices, 95% off gives C$1.50/mo on Standard monthly and C$12.50/yr on Standard yearly. The promotion-code text follows when JF pastes it.

JF's words, verbatim, 2026-09-25: "keep the current pricing, the webhook have been setup for staging webhook." (1) WEBHOOK: JF has set up the Stripe test-mode webhook for staging. Per the checklist it points at https://staging.domiapp.ai/api/stripe/webhook with the five events (customer.subscription.created/updated/deleted, invoice.paid, invoice.payment_failed); chief has not seen the dashboard, so confirm the URL and events against what #2020 serves. The signing secret goes into Vercel staging by JF, never through an agent. (2) PRICING: chief's reading, not JF's words. 'Current pricing' = what is already set up and specced in #2108 (CAD C$30/C$250 and C$50/C$500, Adaptive Pricing, the 95%-off coupon), which JF is confirming unchanged. It does NOT answer the four open DECIDEs (design copy task, upgrade proration, sales tax, past_due); those are still with JF.

UPGRADE Standard -> Plus (answers open DECIDE 'upgrade proration'). JF's words, verbatim, 2026-09-25: "for upgrsding from standr to plus, you charge the difference when that is happening, and it's the new renewal subscripption date". So: charge at the moment of upgrade, and the upgrade date becomes the new renewal date (the billing cycle restarts). CHIEF'S READING in Stripe terms, to verify, not JF's words: subscription update with billing_cycle_anchor=now plus immediate proration invoicing. The customer pays the full Plus period minus a credit for the unused part of Standard. Example: halfway through a C$30 Standard month, the upgrade costs C$50 - C$15 = C$35, and the next renewal is one month after the upgrade day. As far as chief knows, the Stripe customer portal cannot reset the cycle anchor on a same-interval switch, so #2021 may need its own upgrade call rather than portal plan switching. Verify against Stripe's docs. Not covered by this ruling: monthly <-> yearly switches and Plus -> Standard downgrades.

SALES TAX (answers spec §9.2). JF's words, verbatim, 2026-09-25: "sales tax, for now no tax if possible". So: build with NO tax. No Stripe Tax, and no tax lines at checkout. CHIEF'S NOTES, not JF's words: (a) 'for now': keep tax switch-on-able later without re-creating prices, and do not bake a tax assumption into the prices or the UI copy. (b) 'if possible' is a legal condition chief cannot verify. Canadian GST/HST registration is generally required only above the C$30k/yr small-supplier threshold, but with Adaptive Pricing selling abroad, the EU and UK may expect VAT from a foreign seller's first consumer sale. JF will confirm with his accountant before live mode. This does not block the test-mode build.

JF's words, verbatim, 2026-09-25: "A, A, A". Answering the three DECIDEs as chief put them to him:

1. FAILED RENEWAL / past_due (spec §9.1). Chose A: "keep AI on while Stripe retries the card, and cut it off when Stripe gives up". seamCaveat: openRequests counts a request no reply correlates to AND whose thread (contextId) carries nothing later from the recipient. Messages sent before contextId existed have only the first test, so they still OVER-report: treat an open request as a prompt to check, never as proof of a dropped ball. Requests older than the horizon are counted as abandoned, not open.
